reports.verdict: Trump Media's $409.7 million quarterly profit came almost entirely from bitcoin's rise, while the media business stayed tiny and the TAE fusion merger moved closer.

takeaways.label: Profit is bitcoin, not business
takeaways.text: Net income of $409.7 million, versus a $54.8 million loss a year earlier, came mostly from non-cash gains of $496.1 million. The CFO tied the $378.1 million digital-asset gain to a 42% rise in bitcoin.

takeaways.label: Media business still tiny
takeaways.text: Revenue was $3.0 million, up 205%, mostly from the new Truth API data subscription. Adjusted EBITDA was still a $12.3 million loss.

takeaways.label: TAE merger nears vote
takeaways.text: The SEC declared the merger registration effective November 5. Closing is targeted for Q4 2026, pending a Trump Media shareholder vote and regulatory approvals.

takeaways.label: Costs falling
takeaways.text: Operating expenses excluding digital-asset swings were $26.5 million, down 45% from the prior quarter. Legal fees dropped to $2.4 million from $20.3 million a year earlier.

reports.verdict: Berkshire more than doubled buybacks to $9.6 billion as insurance profit dropped, pulling operating earnings down about 6%.

takeaways.label: Buybacks accelerate
takeaways.text: Berkshire repurchased about $9.6 billion of its own stock in the quarter and about $14.4 billion so far this year, a sharp change from the Buffett era.

takeaways.label: Insurance weakens
takeaways.text: Underwriting profit fell 43% to $1.35 billion. Reports say GEICO's pretax profit fell about 45%, so the core insurance business is the main drag on earnings.

takeaways.label: Other businesses grow
takeaways.text: Rail profit rose 19% to $1.73 billion, utilities rose 8% to $1.61 billion, and manufacturing and retail rose to $4.04 billion, which only partly offset insurance.

takeaways.label: Cash pile shrinking
takeaways.text: Berkshire still holds a huge cash pile, reported at roughly $357 billion at quarter-end, but is now spending it on buybacks and the $6.8 billion Taylor Morrison deal.

reports.verdict: EVgo cut its 2026 outlook again, but a $2.00-a-share buyout offer from majority owner LS Power now matters more than the results.

takeaways.label: Buyout offer
takeaways.text: LS Power, which controls about 56% of the vote, proposed buying the rest of the company for $2.00 a share in cash. The offer is non-binding and a special committee is reviewing it.

takeaways.label: Outlook cut again
takeaways.text: 2026 revenue guidance fell to $375-400M from $400-430M, and the adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $15-30M from $5-25M. This is the second cut in a row.

takeaways.label: Core charging is growing
takeaways.text: Charging revenue rose 29% to $72M, but total revenue slipped 1% because partner-built (eXtend) revenue fell 49%. Per-stall usage dropped to 283 kWh a day from 295.

takeaways.label: Losses and cash burn
takeaways.text: Net loss grew to $49M from $28M. Capital spending after offsets rose to $24M from $4M, and cash fell to $99M from $151M at year-end.

reports.verdict: Moderna swung to a profit on international COVID sales and raised its 2026 outlook, but the cash jump is mostly borrowed money.

takeaways.label: Big beat, raised outlook
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 29% to $1.3B against roughly $885M expected, mostly international COVID deals. Full-year growth outlook rose to 15–25% from up to 10%, with net income of $162M.

takeaways.label: Cash boost is borrowed
takeaways.text: Year-end cash outlook jumped to $8.1–8.3B from $4.7–5.2B, helped by $2.6B net from convertible notes. Most Q3 sales were still uncollected, and the nine-month cash burn was $2.7B.

takeaways.label: Cancer vaccine win
takeaways.text: Melanoma vaccine intismeran with Keytruda cut recurrence or death risk 42% in Phase 3. Regulatory filings and launch preparation are underway with Merck.

takeaways.label: Costs falling, flu launch limited
takeaways.text: R&D spending outlook cut to $2.7B from $2.9B. The newly approved flu shot launches only in limited form this season, since approval came after contracting closed.
